text:
jana: Heads-up — saw a lane congestion spike in ap-se1 this morning. Scheduler pushed a bunch of requests into AZ fallback which caused tiny GPU pods to bounce and rebind repeatedly. Anyone oncall?
obrien: I'm here. Noticed attach latency to the NIC near 200-800ms for short-lived pods, scheduler marked nodes degraded -> routed to fallback AZ. Backfill + affinity caused evict loops.
kevin: Oof. Do we have the scheduler decisions? what metric spiked first?
jana: attaching a short excerpt of the event stream I pulled:```
[2026-03-22T08:12:21Z] attach_latency=230ms node=ap-se1a
[2026-03-22T08:12:22Z] scheduler_decision=avoid node=ap-se1a reason=network_attach_latency
[2026-03-22T08:12:23Z] route=ap-se1b fallback=true pod=small-gpu-worker
[2026-03-22T08:12:25Z] eviction=small-gpu-worker node=ap-se1b reason=affinity_conflict
```
jana: full logs sent to #eng-sre (link)
infra-bot: Alert: lane-congestion-ap-se1 detected — 35% degraded nodes in ap-se1 zone, triggered AZ-fallback policy.
sre-oncall: I saw the alert; brief summary — conntrack table exhaustion on a subset of nodes (driver=eni-v2) which increased attach timeouts. When the scheduler sees attach latency > threshold it marks the node transient-unavailable and re-routes. The re-routing saturates target AZ and triggers affinity/taint evictions.
obrien: Interesting — this is a cross-layer failure: kernel conntrack limits -> attach stalls -> scheduler fallback -> packing pressure -> evictions.
kevin: Risk/cost note: fallback is more expensive (inter-AZ egress + double-scheduling). We blew ~6k tokens worth of work? jk 😅 but it did cost us about a full-hour worth of GPU time wasted.
jana: mitigation idea 1: temporary knob — raise attach-latency threshold from 150ms -> 500ms for ap-se1 to reduce false positives while infra patches conntrack. 2: add a small reserved lane (2-3 GPUs) pinned in each AZ for tiny pods so they don't trigger cross-AZ shuffle.
obrien: also propose lowering preempt aggressiveness for pods < 1GPU for 30m window after fallback events. That should reduce churn.
sre-oncall: roll plan: patch autoscaler/scheduler config via canary (5% of traffic) + increase conntrack on problematic nodes via daemonset patch.
kevin: owner volunteers? I can take the scheduler canary (will open PR), @sre-oncall take the daemonset conntrack bump?
sre-oncall: on it. I'll prepare a careful increase (sysctl) — will coordinate with platform to avoid side effects.
jana: I'll watch packing metrics and set an alert on eviction-rate > 3/min for next 2 hours.
obrien: One more long-term ask: can we add a "lane" affinity label that prefers intra-AZ placements for tiny ephemeral GPU pods so the scheduler considers lower-cost intra-AZ placements ahead of fallback?
kevin: that's a good product-ops ask. Let's RFC for lane-affinity and a cost-aware routing policy.
jana: TL;DR: immediate actions = canary scheduler threshold bump (kevin), conntrack sysctl daemonset (sre-oncall), short reserved lane (obrien to triage capacity). I'll follow up with a short postmortem in #postmortems. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline started for scheduler-canary-pr-843.
kevin: PR opened: https://git.company/repo/pull/843 — will monitor.
sre-oncall: conntrack bump rolled to 30% nodes, monitoring for regressions.
jana: seeing reduced attach latency in the canary window. So far so good.
obrien: great. leaving notes for follow-up: add metric for "fallback_rate_by_lane" and a daily job to scan conntrack headroom.
jana: thanks team — keep updates here and move to postmortem after stabilization. :eyes:
